natalie: Quick design Q re: async prefetch for prefix KV. If prefetch writes entries while an inference is reading keys, how do we guarantee we don't return partial/stale states? Thinking about atomic visibility or versioning. Any preferences? :thinking:

samir: I think we need a lightweight epoch/version on each entry. Reader reads value+version, then re-checks version; if changed, either retry or wait. This keeps reads lock-free mostly.

jgonzalez: re: memory pressure - retries could amplify load. Also prefetch might evict entries it just wrote if shared pool pressure spikes. We need a guarantee that prefetch wins for its batch or we accept best-effort caching.

dina: Another option: write into a staging slab and then atomically swap pointer into the main bucket. That gives single-pointer atomicity, no per-key CAS. But requires allocator support.

kevin: Pointer swap sounds neat. But we have prefixes with many keys; swapping per-prefix pointer implies we have to keep contiguous blocks or linked lists. Doable but increases fragmentation.

samir: FWIW here's a pseudo pattern I sketched:

```
// reader
entry = bucket.get(k)
if entry == null return MISS
v = entry.value
ver = entry.version
process(v)
if bucket.get(k).version != ver then goto retry

// writer (prefetch)
newEntry = allocate(value, version=oldver+1)
bucket.cas(k, oldptr, newEntry)
```

natalie: That matches what I had in mind. Two open tradeoffs: (1) read retry cost vs lock contention; (2) complexity of allocator/pointer swap.

jgonzalez: Also think about multi-key atomicity for prefix caching. If we prefetch 100 tokens, do we need them to appear all at once? If not, we can stream them, reducing atomic swap size.

dina: For correctness tests we should add a fuzz test: concurrent reader/writer loops with random evictions and assert no corrupted values (checksum), and no infinite retry loops.

cache-bot: eviction-runner started: shard=17, reclaimed=42 entries, time=3.2s :eyes: 

kevin: Operational note: if we implement version retries, add a metric for retry-rate to the console so we can tune batch sizes.

natalie: Agree. Action items: (1) samir prototype with per-entry versioned CAS, (2) dina adds fuzz test harness, (3) jgonzalez explores allocator-based prefix swaps. I'll follow up with a short RFC update next week. :thumbsup:

samir: I'll push a branch by EOD with microbench results.

dina: I'll wire up a Canary test in CI to run the fuzz harness every PR.

jgonzalez: Filing a small infra ticket about fragmentation limits.

natalie: Thanks everyone — this helped clarify. Closing this thread with notes for the RFC.
